title: Lee2021 – SSVEP paradigm of the Mobile BCI dataset
description: This dataset comprises steady-state visually evoked potential (SSVEP) recordings from 23 healthy participants performing a brain-computer interface (BCI) task during various locomotor states (standing, walking, running). The study employed 73-channel EEG acquisition at 100 Hz sampling rate with three visual flicker stimuli (5.45, 8.57, and 12.0 Hz) presented across 4 sessions per subject. This mobile BCI dataset enables investigation of SSVEP-based neural decoding robustness under dynamic physical conditions.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a 73-channel BrainAmp system (Brain Product GmbH) at 100 Hz sampling rate with Ag/AgCl electrodes referenced to FCz and grounded at Fpz. Participants viewed visual flicker stimuli at three frequencies (5.45, 8.57, 12.0 Hz) during 5-second trials across 4 sessions. The experimental protocol included BCI tasks performed during standing, walking, and running on a treadmill. Signal processing employed rLDA and CCA classifiers with power spectral features extracted from standard frequency bands (delta, theta, alpha, beta).
